subject: history
title: Turning Points of the World Wars
welcome_lead: Today you'll zoom in on the battles and decisions that turned each war.
meta_desc: GCSE History World Wars turning points — Marne, Somme, Stalingrad, D-Day and more.
final_note: You can now explain why certain battles changed the course of each war.

concepts.def: 1914 Allied stand that stopped Germany at Paris
1916 British offensive — huge losses, small gains
1941 German invasion of the Soviet Union
1942-43 Soviet victory that turned the East
7 Dec 1941 Japanese attack — USA entered WWII

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Battle of the Marne in September 1914 stopped the German advance on Paris and began the trench stalemate.

In 1916 the Battle of the Somme cost Britain around 57,000 casualties on day one. In April 1917 the USA joined the Allies — fresh troops tipped the balance.

In June 1941 Hitler launched Operation Barbarossa against the USSR — breaking the Nazi-Soviet Pact.

The Soviets won at Stalingrad in February 1943. D-Day on 6 June 1944 opened a Western Front in France.

Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, bringing the USA into WWII.

The USA won at Midway in 1942 and pushed Japan back island by island. WWII ended after atomic bombs on Hiroshima (6 Aug) and Nagasaki (9 Aug) 1945.

mcqs.q: What were the Wars of the Roses really about?
options: The whole country was at war for thirty continuous years.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Dynastic conflict between rival branches of the Plantagenets (Lancaster and York) over the throne, intensified by weak kingship under Henry VI and noble factionalism.

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
The League failed because no countries joined it.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.

mcqs.q: Why did Britain win the Battle of Britain?
options: Hitler called off the attack to invade the USSR immediately.
The RAF won because Spitfires were better than any German aircraft.
They were a religious war between Catholics and Protestants.
Radar, the Dowding command system, home advantage in pilot recovery, German tactical errors (switching to bombing cities), and adequate fighter production.
